questions.q: Long-range **weather forecasting and nuclear simulation** are typical applications of —
questions.solution: One gigantic scientific computation at a time is the supercomputer's job — weather models, nuclear simulations, space and defence research.

questions.q: PARAM 8000, India's first indigenous supercomputer (1991), was developed by:
questions.solution: PARAM 8000 was built in 1991 by C-DAC (Centre for Development of Advanced Computing), Pune, under Dr Vijay Bhatkar, after the USA denied Cray supercomputer imports.
questions.shortcut: PARAM always pairs with C-DAC; the denial story (' PARAM = Perform Anvaya Reusable Module') is extra trivia - the developer is what SSC asks.

questions.q: The **RJ-45** socket on a computer is used for —
questions.solution: **RJ-45** is the Ethernet port — the tabbed socket that accepts the LAN cable.

questions.q: Entering a single quote followed by SQL code into a login form to manipulate the database is:
questions.solution: SQL injection feeds crafted SQL through input fields so the database executes attacker logic - usually a symptom of unvalidated input.

questions.q: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.solution: **Galloped**: GAL-lop is stressed on the first syllable, so the p stays single. The double l is part of the base word gallop.

questions.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number (1).
questions.solution: After the linking verb *look* (here 'does more than look'), an **adjective** is required: look attractive. *Attractively* is an adverb and cannot follow a linking verb; *attracted* is a verb form and *attraction* a noun, neither of which fits 'look ___' in the sense 'appear'.
questions.shortcut: Linking-verb test: look/sound/seem + adjective, never adverb.
questions.passage: Concrete has conquered our cities, and the first casualty has been the tree. A mature tree on a street does more than look (1) ______: it drops the temperature of its surroundings, traps dust and softens the noise of traffic. Yet when roads are widened, it is usually the tree that (2) ______ way. Municipal budgets treat planting as decoration rather than (3) ______, so saplings are planted in a rush before elections and forgotten soon afterwards. Survival, not planting, is the real (4) ______; a sapling needs watering for three full summers before it can stand on its own. Cities that have understood this simple point now pay residents a small sum to (5) ______ the trees outside their homes — and their streets are visibly greener.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the highlighted segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution required'.

Please **revert back** to my mail by Friday.
questions.solution: **Revert** already means 'come back' → the echo *back* is redundant: 'please **revert to** my mail'. 'Reverting to' breaks the request form; the original keeps the echo.
questions.shortcut: revert, return, repeat — cut the echo word.

questions.q:
Select the option that can substitute the given group of words.

A person who is outgoing and mixes freely with others
questions.solution: extro = outward → interested in what is outside = **extrovert**. An introvert is turned inward; a recluse and a misanthrope avoid people altogether.

questions.q: The **Purna Swaraj** resolution was adopted at the Lahore session of the Congress (1929) presided over by —
questions.solution: **Jawaharlal Nehru** presided over the **Lahore session (December 1929)**, which declared complete independence as the goal; 26 January 1930 was celebrated as Independence Day.

questions.q: Bending of a shoot **towards light** (phototropism) is caused by —
questions.solution: **Auxin** collects on the shaded side and elongates those cells, so the shoot bends toward light. ABA instead closes stomata under stress.

questions.q: **Anaemia** is chiefly caused by the deficiency of —
questions.solution: **Iron** builds the haemoglobin that carries oxygen; low iron → pale, tired, breathless. Vitamin B₁₂ deficiency gives the rarer pernicious anaemia.

questions.q: The successor to the discontinued **Doing Business** rankings is —
questions.solution: **Business Ready (B-READY)**, first released in **2024** by the World Bank, replaced Doing Business.

questions.q: Which of the following is the largest?
questions.solution: $\sin$ increases on $(0^\circ, 90^\circ)$: $\sin 60^\circ = \frac{\sqrt3}{2} \approx 0.87$ beats $\sin 45^\circ \approx 0.71$, $\sin 30^\circ = 0.5$, and $\cos 60^\circ = 0.5$.
questions.shortcut: $\sin 60^\circ$. Trap: $\cos 60^\circ = \sin 30^\circ$ — they tie at $0.5$, well below $\sin 45^\circ$.

questions.q: In a college, 40% of students play cricket, 30% play football and 20% play hockey. 10% play cricket and football, 8% play football and hockey, 6% play cricket and hockey, and 2% play all three. What percentage of students play none of the games?
What is the product of the place values of the two 3s in 53,432?
questions.solution: In 53,432 the first 3 is in the thousands place (3000) and the second is in the tens place (30). Product $= 3000 \times 30 = 90,000$.

questions.q: In an isosceles triangle $ABC$, $AB=AC=25$ cm and $BC=14$ cm. The area of the triangle is:
questions.solution:
The median/altitude to the base: $h=\sqrt{25^2-7^2}=24$ cm.

Area $=\frac12\times14\times24=168\ \text{cm}^2$.
questions.shortcut: 7-24-25 again: height 24, area $=\frac12\times14\times24=168$. Trap: 336 forgot the $\frac12$.

questions.q: **D is 6 km West of C. C is 4 km South of B.** In which direction is **B from D**?
questions.solution: Place D at the origin. 'D is 6 km West of C' puts C 6 km **East** of D. 'C is 4 km South of B' puts B 4 km **North** of C. So B sits at (+6, +4) from D → **North-East** of D.
questions.shortcut: Anchor at D (the asked-from point); C hangs East, B hangs North of C.

questions.q: In a certain code, **PAINT** is written as **UOJBQ**. How is **BRUSH** written in that code?
questions.solution: PAINT reversed = TNIAP; T→U (+1), N→O (+1), I→J (+1), A→B (+1), P→Q (+1) → reverse, then +1. BRUSH reversed = HSURB; +1 → **ITVSC**.
questions.shortcut: First code letter U = T + 1, and T is the last letter of PAINT → reversal + 1.

questions.q:
Three of the following four letter-clusters are alike in a certain way and one is different. Find the odd one out. (The letters follow English alphabetical order.)

**BHL, DJP, FNT, GLR**
questions.solution: Positions: B(2) H(8) L(12); D(4) J(10) P(16); F(6) N(14) T(20) - every letter is at an **even** position. G(7) is odd in GLR → **GLR**.

questions.q: Pointing to a boy, Neha said, **"His mother is the only daughter of my mother."** How is Neha related to the boy?
questions.solution: My mother's only daughter = Neha herself (her mother has exactly one daughter). So the boy's mother **is** Neha → Neha is his **mother**.
questions.shortcut: 'Only daughter of my mother' is the speaker, whenever the speaker is female.
